transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Polaris Head of Platform), Janelle Ruiz (Polaris ML Engineer), Marcus Lee (Polaris Director, IT Ops)

Summary: QBR style health check; main topics were usage, cost trends on hosted, reliability/latency, roadmap items like Dedicated and private deploy, and next steps to run a pilot benchmark.

Topics: usage, cost, reliability, roadmap, security (SOC2/KMS/VPC)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll kick off the QBR. Ethan and I will run through usage and ops highlights, and then we want to sync on next steps for the Dedicated pilot that we discussed last month.
[00:18] Liam: Thanks, Maya. Appetite here is still high, we have a few new integrations shipping next quarter so wanted to understand costs and reliability.
[00:28] Ethan: Great, quick FYI on agenda - usage numbers, tail latency, incidents, cost drivers, then roadmap and pilots.
[00:35] Janelle: Quick callout, we've seen some token spikes around holiday promos, so month-over-month varies a lot.
[00:45] Maya: Right, Janelle we pulled the last three months - average ~120M tokens/month, peak days up to 6M, cost on hosted has been increasing because of repeated rerank and long context sessions.
[01:05] Janelle: Yea, we run longer context for session histories which hits cost. We were thinking quantization or a smaller model for some paths.
[01:12] Ethan: That's a common tradeoff - latency vs cost. With Dedicated you get predictable throughput and cost per token goes down, also we can suggest quant profiles where accuracy stays comparable.
[01:26] Marcus: On reliability we had that spike last month - about a 10-minute elevated error period, do you have logs on that?
[01:34] Maya: We do, we linked the incident to regional capacity pressure and automatic fallback occurred, so some requests routed to a slightly different variant which caused higher 5xx rate for a short window. We logged trace ids and will share the incident report.
[01:50] Liam: Right, again the fallback was okay but it impacted our SLAs. If Dedicated avoids that, it's attractive.
[02:00] Ethan: For Dedicated we can reserve GPU pools for your commits, plus burst capacity. That reduces noisy neighbor issues; we also support routing policy to prefer pinned model versions.
[02:12] Janelle: Can you remind me about KV cache behavior - we rely on prefix cache for chat sessions.
[02:18] Ethan: Sure - we have prefix/KV caching on the serving runtime; on Dedicated you get warmer KV caches per pool and lower cold-cache overhead. There's also configurable TTLs and we can snapshot hot keys during scale events.
[02:36] Janelle: Cool, any gotchas with our current infra? We use a VPC peering setup for auth and have strict egress rules.
[02:44] Maya: For Private or Dedicated VPC, we support customer-managed networking and peering. We'll need Marcus's network firewall CIDRs and the port list; we'll share a checklist.
[02:58] Marcus: Yeah, I'll pull that. Also need to confirm KMS flow - we require a customer-managed KMS for some data.
[03:06] Ethan: We integrate with KMS/HSM; we can do envelope encryption and KMS for workspace keys. We'll attach the relevant architecture doc and the SOC 2 snapshot.
[03:18] Liam: Great. Circle back to costs - can you break down what's driving the month-to-month increase?
[03:25] Maya: Sure - primary drivers are increased avg tokens per session from the new recommendation flows, reranking calls per user doubled due to A/B experiments, and longer context windows. We also saw a couple of background batch jobs hitting the API inadvertently.
[03:43] Janelle: Oops, that'll be on us, we have a cron that replays queries for retraining - we can throttle that.
[03:50] Maya: If you can gate those batch jobs that's immediate savings. Longer term, Dedicated plus batching/caching configs and some quantization will reduce unit costs; our Optimize recommendations will show you expected delta.
[04:05] Liam: Do you have a sample estimate for Dedicated cost per token vs hosted?
[04:11] Maya: We'll send an updated pricing sheet. Ballpark, for your volume, Dedicated could reduce per-token unit cost by 20-35% depending on commit and burst settings. We'll model it in the proposal.
[04:24] Marcus: For the pilot - how long, what metrics do we run?
[04:29] Ethan: Recommend a 2-week benchmark window: measure p50/p95 latency, successful response rate, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll need representative prompt sets and traffic shape from you.
[04:42] Janelle: We can provide ~500 prompts and 3 typical traffic curves: baseline, promo spike, and night-batch.
[04:51] Maya: Perfect. We'll schedule a workshop to align on dataset and the benchmark harness.
[04:56] Liam: On security docs - can you share SOC 2 and evidence around audit logs?
[05:02] Maya: Yes - we'll share SOC 2 summary, audit log retention options, and our RBAC/SSO patterns. Also include the KMS integration doc.
[05:12] Janelle: Any limitations we should watch for with on-prem/private? Latency to internal services is a concern.
[05:19] Ethan: On-prem installs can be run with a private control plane; latency depends on your internal network. We do offer hybrid models where control plane sits in our cloud and inference runs in your VPC. We'll outline network topology options.
[05:33] Liam: Nice. A few product Qs - any roadmap items that will impact us?
[05:38] Maya: Short term roadmap: better cost observability (token breakouts per route), improved batching heuristics, and GA of the Dedicated autoscaler enhancements. Mid-term: private on-prem automation and expanded quantization profiles.
[05:52] Janelle: For observability, we want token-level breakdown per route - helps attribute cost to teams.
[05:58] Ethan: That's in the pipeline; we can prioritize in your account roadmap.
[06:03] Marcus: SLA - if we commit to Dedicated, what's the uptime and latency SLO?
[06:09] Maya: We offer SLA-backed uptime and target latency bands based on config. We'll include the SLA terms in the Dedicated proposal.
[06:17] Liam: Great. Any compliance red flags with our PCI-ish flows?
[06:21] Ethan: For PCI we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with strict network controls and tokenization at the edge. We'll draft recommended architecture.
[06:32] Janelle: Back to action - we should get the benchmark running before the promo season in 3 weeks.
[06:38] Maya: Agreed - timeline: pricing and docs by 2/12, benchmark workshop week of 2/16, pilot window 2/23-3/8.
[06:48] Liam: Works for me.
[06:51] Marcus: I'll send firewall info and KMS contacts.
[06:54] Janelle: I'll send the prompt set and traffic curves.
[07:00] Maya: OK quick recap and next steps - we'll send the detailed pricing + Dedicated proposal, SOC2/KMS docs, and the benchmark plan template. Ethan will set the workshop invite. Polaris to send prompts and infra details.
[07:14] Liam: Thanks folks. That was useful.
[07:18] Maya: Thanks everyone.

Post-meeting notes:
- Incident report link and trace ids to be shared by Maya (note: referenced in email thread)
- Proposal will include commit tiers and burst pricing, plus modeled savings for 120M tokens/month usage
- Benchmark plan will include three traffic shapes, 500 prompts, p95/p50 latency, error rate, and cost per 1k tokens metrics

Action items (restate):
- Maya: send pricing + Dedicated proposal, SOC2/KMS docs (due 2026-02-12)
- Ethan: prepare benchmark harness + schedule workshop (due 2026-02-17)
- Janelle: provide prompt set and traffic curves (due 2026-02-14)
- Marcus: provide network CIDRs and KMS contacts (due 2026-02-18)

References shared in chat: pricing spreadsheet link (sent in chat), incident log link (to be posted), SOC2 summary (will be sent).

End of transcript.
